h: Deer etiquette, war stories and Altrincham bites
p: Dunham Massey has a surprising wartime chapter. During the First World War, part of the house became the Stamford Military Hospital, where injured soldiers were nursed back to health. The family themselves helped with the work, and it's a moving side of the story that brings a different perspective to a grand stately home.

The deer are the stars for most visitors, and there are a few simple rules to keep both them and you safe. Don't feed them, give them plenty of space and keep dogs on a short lead in the deer park. Autumn is rutting season, when the stags can get a bit lively, so it's a time to watch from a distance. Early mornings and quieter weekdays are best for spotting the herd going about their business.

Allow half a day to explore the garden and a decent loop of the park, or longer if you're doing the house. The paths are mostly flat, which makes it good for pushchairs and for anyone who prefers an easier walk. It gets very busy on sunny weekends and bank holidays, so arriving early is a smart move.

The Bridgewater Canal runs past the edge of the estate, so you can stretch your legs along the towpath if you fancy more of a walk. Afterwards, Altrincham is just a few minutes away. The town has built a real reputation for food, with Altrincham Market and its indoor food hall a popular spot for lunch or a relaxed evening. The Metrolink tram connects Altrincham with central Manchester, so it's easy to combine with a city trip.
